sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year from $37.8 billion in FY2017 to $67.4 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F196].
The path was flat for five years, then stepped up 17.7% in FY2023 and 17.3% in FY2026 [D280][D421].
The FY2023 step came from the Cerner acquisition, which added $5.9 billion of revenue, 11.8% of the year's total [S61][D604][P48].
FY2026's step was cloud-led: cloud and software revenue rose $9.3 billion as customers bought applications and infrastructure and renewed cloud contracts [P17][P20].
Cloud Infrastructure is now the growth engine, contributing 13.7pp of the 17.3% revenue growth in FY2026 on 76.9% growth [D645][D421][D644].
It reached 26.9% of revenue, while Software Support slipped to 29.4% and Software License fell 8.9% [D643][D613][D681].
The Americas supplied 14.2pp of FY2026 growth and 66.0% of revenue, with the U.S. alone at 59.1% [D470][D468][D484].
Operating income grew 16.6% against 17.3% revenue growth, so incremental margin was 29.4% and operating expenses grew 17.7% [D422][D421][D442][D436].
Diluted EPS grew 34.3% against 36.5% net income growth as the diluted share count rose 1.7% [D425][D423][D438].
Operating margin was 30.6% in FY2026, below the 32.2% window median and well under the 37.6% FY2021 high [F34][D788][D787].
The margin fell 0.2pp as operating expenses rose 17.7%, driven by a $6.0 billion increase in cloud and software expenses from higher infrastructure costs [D433][D436][P19].
Selling and marketing fell to 12.4% of revenue from 15.1%, and R&D fell to 15.3% from 17.2%, offsetting that cost pressure [D400][D353][D399][D352].
The largest move was FY2022, when operating margin fell 11.8pp on litigation charges recorded to acquisition related and other expenses [D246][P58].
Net margin rose 3.5pp to 25.2% as the effective tax rate fell to 28.4% from 39.2%, helped by $1.5 billion more stock-based compensation tax benefit [D434][F54][D407][D360][P9].
Operating cash flow rose 53.6% to $32.0 billion, 47.5% of revenue, on higher net income and $4.6 billion of customer prepayments [D426][F84][D406][P6].
Free cash flow was negative $23.7 billion, a -35.2% margin, as capex reached $55.7 billion, 82.6% of revenue [F104][D405][F94][D404].
Capex rose $34.4 billion, taking capex to 7.30x D&A, as the company built data center capacity [P5][D410].
Free cash flow was -1.39x net income against a 1.06x window median, and operating cash flow covered net income 1.88x [D409][D800][D408].
Net debt reached $97.6 billion, 145.0% of revenue, the 0th percentile of six software peers [D414][D415][D815].
Total debt rose 39.9% to $129.5 billion on $42.7 billion of senior notes issued in FY2026 [D440][D413][P7].
Cash and investments rose 184.7% to $31.9 billion, leaving the current ratio at 1.12x against a 1.96x median [D439][D412][F184][D803].
Buybacks plus dividends were $5.9 billion, with repurchases down to $95 million and dividends at $5.8 billion [D416][X155][X165].
Cash and investments cover only 1.3 years of the latest $23.7 billion burn, and $260 billion of data center lease commitments sit off balance sheet [D419][D418][P1].
Free cash flow fell below net income for two years, at -0.03x in FY2025 and -1.39x in FY2026 [D362][D409].
Net debt rose two years running, from $76.2 billion in FY2024 to $97.6 billion in FY2026 [D320][D414].
The FY2026 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K figure by up to 0.60%; the 10-K shows $17.1 billion [F44][X20][R5].
Free cash flow margin: a return above the 26.0% window median would confirm the capex cycle is peaking, while another year near -35.2% would extend the burn [D794][D792].
Operating margin: holding above the 30.6% latest level would show infrastructure costs scaling, while a drop toward the 25.7% FY2022 low would reverse the recovery [F34][D786].
Net debt: any move below the $97.6 billion FY2026 level would ease the leverage concern, while further growth would keep it at the peer bottom [D414][D815].
